name: sersniff
desc: Program to tunnel/sniff between 2 serial ports
why: Tunnels and sniffs traffic between two serial ports, a direct way to watch a physical device talk.

brief.what_it_is: sersniff is a small command-line program that sits between two serial ports and tunnels traffic between them while sniffing it, so you can see what passes in each direction. The page says it can also sniff a TCP connection or bridge a serial port to a TCP port. The homepage gives version 0.0.5 and offers a source tarball of about 16kb. It does not document command-line usage, options, or output format.
brief.why_it_exists: The author, Jonathan McDowell, wrote it to help decode the protocol the Nokia 9000i Communicator uses to talk to Nokia's NServer software, which only runs under Windows. He released it because others might need something similar and a skeleton could help.
brief.install_notes: The homepage lists only a source tarball, so installation likely means building from source. No build steps, dependencies, or configuration are described on the page. Brew installs the executable named sersniff.
brief.standout: It is a tiny, purpose-built tool that started as a reverse-engineering aid for one old phone protocol. The author explicitly invites others to extend it into a framework of filters, like ethernet sniffers have, for disassembling unknown serial protocols.
brief.status: quiet. The page says 'Last updated: Sat Jul  9 18:58:24 BST 2011' and the current version is 0.0.5. I did not check a repository or release history, so I cannot say whether it is actively maintained.
brief.caveats: The page documents no usage, flags, or example commands. It is a simple skeleton, and the author says filters and a wider framework may never be written. The description says the program was 'hastily thrown together'. Licensed under the GNU GPL. The page is the only source I read, so platform support and build requirements are unverified.
